Stand down on new credit spreads today, or push DTE past the vol spike; this is not a premium-selling tape.

focus.jtag: Thursday's AI/chip meltdown sent the S&P down 4.36% (worst day since April 2025) and the VIX up ~70% to 28.18. Friday futures try to stabilize (S&P ~+0.3%, Nasdaq ~+1.5%) into the October jobs report at 8:30 ET. The scanner boarded 6 Type A gaps (ABNB, IREN, MNST, MCD, ZTS, VST) and 1 Type C breakout (PG)
focus.jnote: Thursday broke the tape; Friday is trying to repair it — but the damage is real. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% on November 5, 2026, the Nasdaq fell 5.52%, and the Dow dropped 3.44%, showing heavier pressure on technology-sensitive shares. Stocks plunged as AI and chip names were sold off, more than erasing Wednesday's post-election rally, and the Nasdaq Composite fell into correction territory. The fear gauge exploded: the VIX closed up 69.7% at 28.17, its biggest one-day percentage gain since December 18, 2024. Friday is a bounce attempt — US stock futures attempted to stabilize after a post-election rally turned into an AI trade meltdown, with S&P 500 futures up 0.3% and Nasdaq buyers moving in. But the big overhang is data: the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the jobs report at 8:30 am ET on Friday, November 6, with economists expecting about 59,000–65,000 new jobs and unemployment near 4.2%. A Fed-watched print into a VIX-28 tape is exactly the setup a Sniper does not sell premium into.
focus.notdown: Of the boarded bullish names, the defensive staple PG and the big-beat gaps ABNB and IREN are the least-bad fits for a shell-shocked tape — but none is a clean Sniper today. Airbnb beat Wall Street's revenue expectations in Q3, with revenue up 18.9% to $4.87 billion and GAAP profit 11% above estimates. IREN beat too, but it said some revenue is being delayed from 2026 until early next year after a dramatic plunge in its stock price. With the VIX at ~28 and a jobs print pending, every one is watch-only, A-grade and confirmed-at-9:35 only — and the honest answer today is to sell nothing new.
focus.notup: The bearish Type A gaps (MNST, MCD, ZTS) and the breakdown name VST have fundamental logic, but selling bear calls into a VIX-28, post-crash bounce is squeeze-prone. VST is the clearest down story: Vistra faces a sharp policy-driven selloff after Texas elected a governor who supports pausing new data-center development, and its November 6 earnings report could clarify whether contracted power demand protects near-term earnings. But a relief bounce off a 4%+ market drop can rip shorts violently on any good-news headline — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Three independent locks: composite 72 is in HOT (≥70 = stand down), P(≥1% gap) at 52% is well above the 35% trigger, and the October jobs report lands at 8:30 ET — a Fed-watched print that forbids GREEN on its own. On top of that, the VIX just posted its biggest one-day jump since December 2024, and a one-day 70% vol spike leaves an unstable, headline-whippy tape. Stand down on new credit spreads, or if you must be positioned, push DTE out past the vol spike and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: October jobs report · 8:30 ET today — economists expect the U.S. to have added about 59,000 new jobs in October with unemployment near 4.2%; a hot or cold surprise into a VIX-28 tape gaps the whole market. This is the number-one thing to watch.

AI/chip-regulation aftershock — stocks plunged as AI and chip names were sold off on data-center-regulation fears, with the Nasdaq entering correction. Any follow-through selling re-arms the second leg down.

Volatility spike & vol-of-vol — the VIX jumped 69.7% to 28.17 and the VVIX jumped 49.3% to 134.99, its biggest one-day gain since February 2007. A spike this acute leaves the tape unstable and squeeze-prone in both directions.
December rate-hike odds in flux — traders now see a 68% chance of a December rate rise, down from near certainty last month; the jobs print will re-price that and whip rates and risk intraday.
Single-stock earnings gaps — ABNB, IREN, MNST, ZTS, VST and MCD all just reported; on a HOT day those names can gap violently on any headline, stacking single-stock risk on top of the index.
